[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"SQL Ranking Functions: ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), and DENSE_RANK()"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQL ranking functions are essential tools for assigning ranks to rows within a result set based on specified criteria. These functions provide a way to analyze data and identify top performers, outliers, or specific data points within a dataset. The three most commonly used ranking functions are ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), and DENSE_RANK(). This tutorial will provide a comprehensive overview of each function, including syntax, examples, and practical use cases."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"ROW_NUMBER()"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The ROW_NUMBER() function assigns a unique sequential integer to each row within a partition of a result set. The row number starts at 1 for the first row in each partition.  It's important to note that ROW_NUMBER() assigns a unique number even if rows have identical values in the ordering column(s)."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Syntax"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( [PARTITION BY column1, column2, ...] ORDER BY column3 [ASC | DESC], ... )"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PARTITION BY (optional): Divides the result set into partitions. The ROW_NUMBER() function is applied to each partition independently."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ORDER BY: Specifies the order in which rows are assigned numbers within each partition. This is mandatory."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Example"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a table named 'Employees' with columns 'EmployeeID', 'Department', and 'Salary'.  We want to assign a unique row number to each employee within each department, ordered by salary in descending order."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT
    EmployeeID,
    Department,
    Salary,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Department ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS RowNum
FROM
    Employees;"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, the 'PARTITION BY Department' clause divides the employees into groups based on their department. The 'ORDER BY Salary DESC' clause orders the employees within each department by salary in descending order. The ROW_NUMBER() function then assigns a unique number to each employee within each department, starting from 1 for the employee with the highest salary in that department."},{"order":13,"type":"heading","text":"RANK()"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"The RANK() function assigns a rank to each row within a partition of a result set based on the order of the specified column(s). Unlike ROW_NUMBER(), RANK() assigns the same rank to rows with equal values in the ordering column(s). The next rank is then skipped, resulting in gaps in the ranking sequence."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Syntax"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"RANK() OVER ( [PARTITION BY column1, column2, ...] ORDER BY column3 [ASC | DESC], ... )"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PARTITION BY (optional): Divides the result set into partitions. The RANK() function is applied to each partition independently."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ORDER BY: Specifies the order in which rows are assigned ranks within each partition. This is mandatory."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Example"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Using the same 'Employees' table, we want to assign a rank to each employee within each department based on their salary, with employees earning the same salary receiving the same rank."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"SELECT
    EmployeeID,
    Department,
    Salary,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Department ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS Rank
FROM
    Employees;"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, if two employees in the same department have the same salary, they will both receive the same rank. If they are ranked '2', the next employee will be ranked '4', skipping '3'."},{"order":23,"type":"heading","text":"DENSE_RANK()"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"The DENSE_RANK() function is similar to RANK(), but it assigns consecutive ranks without gaps, even when there are ties in the ordering column(s).  If multiple rows have the same value, they receive the same rank, and the next rank assigned is the next consecutive integer."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Syntax"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"DENSE_RANK() OVER ( [PARTITION BY column1, column2, ...] ORDER BY column3 [ASC | DESC], ... )"},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PARTITION BY (optional): Divides the result set into partitions. The DENSE_RANK() function is applied to each partition independently."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ORDER BY: Specifies the order in which rows are assigned ranks within each partition. This is mandatory."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Example"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Again, using the 'Employees' table, we want to assign a rank to each employee within each department based on their salary, ensuring that the ranks are consecutive even if multiple employees have the same salary."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"SELECT
    EmployeeID,
    Department,
    Salary,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Department ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS DenseRank
FROM
    Employees;"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, if two employees in the same department have the same salary, they will both receive the same rank. If they are ranked '2', the next employee will be ranked '3', not skipping any numbers."},{"order":33,"type":"heading","text":"Comparison and Use Cases"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's a table summarizing the key differences between the three ranking functions:"},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ROW_NUMBER(): Assigns a unique sequential integer to each row. Use when you need a unique identifier for each row within a partition, regardless of ties."},{"order":36,"type":"bullet_point","text":"RANK(): Assigns ranks with gaps for ties. Use when you want to identify the relative position of rows, and gaps in the ranking are acceptable."},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DENSE_RANK(): Assigns consecutive ranks without gaps. Use when you want to identify the relative position of rows, and you need consecutive ranks even with ties."},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"Common use cases include identifying top performers (e.g., top 10 sales representatives), calculating percentiles, and generating reports that require ranked data."},{"order":39,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), and DENSE_RANK() are powerful SQL functions that provide flexible ways to rank data within a result set. Understanding the differences between these functions and their appropriate use cases is crucial for effective data analysis and reporting. By mastering these functions, you can gain valuable insights from your data and make more informed decisions."}]
